ex.en: I play volleyball with friends every weekend.
Did you watch the volleyball game last night?
Our daughter joined the volleyball team at school.

note: 담배를 피우다 = to smoke cigarettes.

ex.en: You can't smoke here.

ex.s: 아빠가 담배를 끊고 이제 안 피워요.
ex.en: Dad quit smoking and doesn't smoke anymore.
We lit a campfire at the campsite.
Shall we each pay for ourselves today?
Everyone bring your own snacks.
We each have our own room.
I'll join you after work.
Minho is joining the trip tomorrow too.
A new team member joins next week.

note: 감염되다 = to get infected.

ex.en: Be careful so the cut doesn't get infected.

ex.s: 바이러스 감염을 막으려면 손을 자주 씻으세요.
ex.en: Wash your hands often to prevent viral infection.
My computer got a virus.

note: 증가하다 = to increase.

ex.en: Tourists have increased a lot lately.
I started exercising because of weight gain.
Orders suddenly went up, so we're busy.

note: A different 영감 means 'old man' (casual).

ex.en: I got new inspiration while traveling.
This song was inspired by my mom.
Where do you get your design inspiration?
Want to go to the art museum together this weekend?
The art museum is closed on Mondays.

ex.s: 파리에 가면 미술관부터 가 보고 싶어요.
ex.en: When I go to Paris, I want to see the art museums first.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 구워요, 구운.

ex.en: Let's grill some meat for dinner tonight.
Mom baked the birthday cake herself.
I baked the bread too long and it burned.
My stamina has really dropped lately.
You need good stamina to go hiking.
You need energy to play with kids.
Our company is running an environmental campaign.
I took part in an anti-smoking campaign at school.
This ad campaign is getting a good response.
Is there anything in particular you want to eat?
Today it's a special treat — I'll pay.

ex.s: 특별히 할 일 없으면 같이 영화 봐요.
ex.en: If you've got nothing in particular to do, let's watch a movie.
Ji-woo has a really outgoing personality.
Our puppy is liveliest in the morning.
This club is very active.

en: on purpose; go out of one's way

ex.en: I didn't do it on purpose. Sorry.
Thank you for coming all this way.
I take the stairs on purpose to lose weight.

note: 르-irregular: 길러요. 키우다 is a common synonym.

ex.en: I have two cats.
I'm growing my hair out these days.
I grow tomatoes on the balcony.

note: 예상하다 = to expect; 예상보다 = than expected.

ex.en: There are way more people than expected.
My guess was right.
I expected it would rain tomorrow.
They're twins, so it's hard to tell them apart.
Be sure to sort your trash before throwing it out.
Can you tell wines apart by taste?
More ice, please.
There's ice on the road, so it's slippery.
Put ice on where you got hurt.
I hurt my back yesterday while moving.
These pants are a little big in the waist.
My back hurts if I sit for a long time.

note: From English 'ID'. An ID card is 신분증.

ex.en: I forgot my username and password.
What's your game username?
It says this username is already taken.
This fruit is rich in vitamins.
That teacher has a lot of experience.
My friend has really expressive faces.
If you add 3 to 2, you get 5.
It tastes better if you add a little salt.
You have to add shipping to this price.
Hundreds of people came to the concert.
I've heard that story hundreds of times.

ex.s: 여행 가서 사진을 수백 장 찍었어요.
ex.en: I took hundreds of photos on the trip.

note: 르-irregular: 찔러요; 찔리다 = to get pricked.

ex.en: I pricked my finger on a rose thorn.
My friend poked me in the side.
The smell from the kitchen stings my nose.
Deserts get really cold at night.
I did a desert tour in Egypt.
I rode a camel in the desert.

ex.s: 저 큰 바위 위에서 사진 찍어요.
ex.en: Let's take a picture on that big rock.
The rocks are slippery, so be careful.
We sat on a rock by the beach and rested.

note: 대결하다 = to face off.

ex.s: 오늘 밤에 한국 대 일본 대결이 있어요.
ex.en: There's a Korea vs. Japan showdown tonight.
I had a game showdown with my brother and lost.
Let's have a cooking contest!

note: Used after a number: 10분 이내.

ex.en: I'll arrive within 10 minutes.

ex.s: 구매 후 7일 이내에 교환할 수 있어요.
ex.en: You can exchange it within 7 days of purchase.
There's a station within a 5-minute walk of home.

note: 핑크색 and 분홍색 are both used.

ex.en: The pink dress looks good on you.
My daughter likes pink the most.
I bought pink lipstick since it's spring.
I convinced Mom, so we got to have a dog.
Convincing the team leader isn't easy.
I persuaded my friend to work out with me.

ex.s: 이거 샘플 좀 받을 수 있어요?
ex.en: Could I get a sample of this?
The cosmetics shop gave me lots of samples.

ex.s: 회의 전에 디자인 샘플을 보내 주세요.
ex.en: Please send the design samples before the meeting.
What's this button for?
I bought this bag for traveling.
We use this room as storage.
There's an old grave inside the park.
This is an ancient king's tomb.
I placed flowers in front of Grandma's grave.
The cat is eyeing the fish.
We're aiming to win this match.
I'm going to wait for the sale to buy it.
Red berries have grown on this tree.
Is this berry safe to eat?
It's fall, so the persimmon tree is full of fruit.

note: 몸 is the everyday word.

ex.en: The physical exam is tomorrow morning.
Exercise is good for your physical health.

ex.s: 이 서류에 키 같은 신체 정보를 써 주세요.
ex.en: Please write body info like height on this form.
Can you speak Chinese?
I'm learning Chinese from Wei these days.
The menu is only written in Chinese.

note: 다이어트하다 = to be on a diet.

ex.en: I'm on a diet these days.
Because of my diet, I only eat salad for dinner.
I'll start my diet tomorrow!
Personality matters more than looks.
I look a lot like my older brother.

ex.s: 면접 때는 외모에도 신경 써야 해요.
ex.en: You should pay attention to your appearance at interviews too.
The kid broke the toy again.
We knocked down a wall and made the living room bigger.
Crush the ice and put it in the drink.

note: Opposite: 불리하다. Not related to 유리 (glass).

ex.en: Good English gives you an edge in job hunting.
Going early gives you a better shot at a seat.
It's a home game, so our team has the advantage.
My phone's memory is full.

ex.s: 여행 가기 전에 카메라 메모리를 비웠어요.
ex.en: I cleared my camera's memory before the trip.
I want to upgrade my computer's memory.
You shouldn't keep putting off your homework.
We postponed the meeting to next week.
We put off the picnic because of the rain.
This photo is my treasure.
We did a treasure hunt with the kids.
Grandma's ring is our family treasure.

note: Honorific: used for elders, guests, bosses.

ex.en: I'm taking my parents on a trip this weekend.
Please show the guest to the meeting room.
I took Grandma to the hospital.

note: An everyday dress is 원피스.

ex.en: I'm choosing a wedding dress.
What dress are you wearing to the party?
I borrowed this dress from a friend.

note: 빚지다 = to owe; 빚을 갚다 = to repay.

ex.en: I finally paid off all my debt!
I don't want to owe my friend money.
Thanks for helping. I owe you one.
I booked a room with a double bed.
An Americano with a double shot, please.
This week you earn double points.
My family was poor when I was little.
I'm a broke student, so I spend carefully.
That movie is about a poor family.

note: Used as 과학적인 + noun, or 과학적으로.

ex.en: That's been scientifically proven.
Is there scientific evidence for that?
My kid asks a lot of science questions.
This has to be washed by hand.
I washed the comforter over the weekend.
The baby is sucking her finger.

note: Fish as food is 생선.

ex.en: There are lots of fish in the river.
My son says he wants to keep fish.
I saw fish while snorkeling in the ocean.

note: 1+1 (원 플러스 원) = buy one, get one free.

ex.en: Experience is a plus.
It's cheap, so that's a plus.
These snacks are buy one, get one free.
For details, contact customer service.
I contacted the hotel about my reservation.
I called to ask about the price.
I'm working out consistently every day.
If you study Korean steadily, you'll improve.
That shop gets customers steadily.

note: Mostly used by women. 어머나 is stronger.

ex.en: Oh my, long time no see!
Oh, this is so pretty!
Oh no, I left my wallet behind.
I prepared thoroughly for the exam.
That restaurant is strict about hygiene.
Our team leader is a really meticulous person.
Let's dance together at the wedding!
I like dancing.
The kids are dancing to the song.
This is your share, Ji-woo.
I ate my little brother's share too.
Doing the dishes is my job.

note: 샤워하다 = to take a shower.

ex.en: I showered after working out.
I usually shower in the morning.
The shower in the hotel room is broken.
What page in the textbook?
I left my textbook at home.
Kevin teaches Korean using an English textbook.

note: 장난해요? = Are you kidding me?

ex.en: The kids are playing around with water.
Don't goof around in class.
Are you kidding? That's way too expensive!

note: Spelled 왠지, not 웬지.

ex.en: For some reason I want to go to bed early tonight.
Somehow it feels like it's going to rain.
That person looks familiar somehow.
I'll get there as fast as I can.
Pack as light as possible for the trip.
I'm saving as much money as I can these days.
Our dog has gotten pretty old now.
I want to stay healthy even when I'm old.
Stress makes you age fast.
What does this sign mean?
A red light means stop.
This emoji means laughing.

note: 하드 = 하드디스크; also a bar-style ice pop.

ex.en: I backed up my photos to an external hard drive.
My work computer's hard drive died.

ex.s: 더워서 편의점에서 하드 하나 사 먹었어요.
ex.en: It was hot, so I bought an ice pop at the convenience store.
The air is so dry in winter.
My skin is dry, so I put on lotion.
It's really dry on the plane.

note: A different 짜다 (adjective) means salty: 국이 짜요.

ex.en: Squeeze some lemon juice and add it.
We planned the trip itinerary together.
I squeezed out too much toothpaste.

note: Humble form of 보다. 뵈어요 → 봬요. 뵙다 is more formal.

ex.en: See you tomorrow, then!
I'm going to my hometown to see my parents.
I'll see you at next week's meeting.
Minho is really smart.

ex.s: 우리 강아지는 똑똑해서 말을 잘 알아들어요.
ex.en: Our dog is smart and understands us well.
I want to be a smart shopper.
This magic trick is amazing!

ex.s: 아기가 처음 걸었을 때 너무 신기했어요.
ex.en: It was amazing when the baby first walked.
Korean convenience stores have lots of fun, unusual stuff.
The cat ran off as soon as I opened the door.
I saw a bug and ran away screaming.
I have so much homework I want to run away.

note: As food: 닭고기; fried chicken is 치킨.

ex.en: Grandma raises chickens in the countryside.
Tonight's dinner is spicy braised chicken.
I woke up at dawn to a rooster crowing.
I bought fruit, bread, milk, and so on.

ex.s: 청소, 빨래, 요리 등등 할 일이 많아요.
ex.en: Cleaning, laundry, cooking — there's lots to do.

ex.s: 축구, 수영, 테니스 등등 다 좋아해요.
ex.en: I like soccer, swimming, tennis, all of it.

note: Trendy: 감성 카페 = a café with a stylish, cozy vibe.

ex.en: This café has such an aesthetic vibe.
That singer is very emotionally expressive.

ex.s: 밤에 이 노래 들으면 감성에 젖어요.
ex.en: Listening to this song at night makes me sentimental.
The weather is gradually getting warmer.
I'm gradually getting used to the new job.
After the medicine, the pain gradually eased.
Let's meet at a bar near the office.
This bar has really good food to go with drinks.
The bar was too loud, so we stepped outside.
Can you help me fold the laundry?
Please close your umbrella before coming in.
I folded paper airplanes with my kid.

note: 졸업하다 = to graduate.

ex.en: Congratulations on your graduation!
I got a job right after graduating from college.
My younger sibling's graduation ceremony is next month.
My friend is a fashion designer.
I asked a designer to make a logo.
A famous designer made this bag.

note: 할인하다 = to give a discount.

ex.en: Is there a student discount?
If you buy now, you get 30% off.
I'd like to use a discount coupon.
The teacher's explanation was very clear.
Please say clearly what you want.
The cause of the breakdown isn't clear yet.
I had bread and coffee for breakfast.
This neighborhood bakery is really good.
I'll run to the convenience store for some bread.

note: Opposite: 단점 (weakness, drawback).

ex.en: What do you think your strengths are?

ex.s: 이 집의 장점은 역이 가깝다는 거예요.
ex.en: The upside of this place is that it's close to the station.
My friend has a lot of good qualities.

en: to recall; to come up with
note: Intransitive form: 떠오르다 (to come to mind).

ex.en: I came up with a good idea.

ex.s: 이 노래를 들으면 대학 시절을 떠올리게 돼요.
ex.en: This song makes me think back to my college days.

ex.s: 그 사람 이름을 떠올리려고 했는데 생각이 안 나요.
ex.en: I tried to recall that person's name, but it won't come.

ex.s: 귀신 나오는 영화는 무서워서 못 봐요.
ex.en: I can't watch ghost movies — they're too scary.
They say a ghost lives in that house.
We went into the haunted house at the amusement park.

note: 집중하다 = to concentrate.

ex.en: It's noisy, so I can't concentrate.
Please focus on the meeting.
I focus better when I drink coffee.

en: to have a hard time; work hard
note: 고생하셨어요 = Thanks for your hard work.

ex.en: Thanks for all your hard work today.
I got lost and had a rough time for a while.
I suffered with a cold for a whole week.

note: 협력하다 = to cooperate.

ex.en: Thanks to everyone's cooperation, we finished early.

ex.s: 이 프로젝트는 다른 팀과 협력해서 해요.
ex.en: We're doing this project together with another team.
The neighbors worked together to clear the snow.

note: 승인하다 = to approve; 승인되다 = to be approved.

ex.en: My vacation finally got approved.
My card was declined.
Visa approval takes two weeks.

note: Grave sense is a different word, used for family graves.

ex.en: There's less oxygen high up in the mountains.
Plants produce oxygen.
We visited Grandpa's grave on Lunar New Year.

note: 지적하다 = to point out. A different 지적 means intellectual.

ex.en: Thanks for pointing out my mistake.
I got called out by the team leader today.
The teacher pointed out my pronunciation.

note: 지시하다 = to instruct.

ex.en: Take the medicine as the doctor instructed.
I'm waiting for my boss's instructions.
Please follow the flight attendants' instructions.

note: 재다 is the everyday word.

ex.en: I measure my blood pressure every morning.
I track my steps with this app.
They took our temperature at the airport.

note: Used as 전형적인 + noun.

ex.en: It's a typical Korean breakfast.
That's a classic dad joke.
Today is typical fall weather.
Lately I feel the need to exercise.

ex.s: 저는 차를 살 필요성을 못 느껴요.
ex.en: I don't feel any need to buy a car.
In the meeting we discussed the need for a new hire.

note: 신분증 = ID card.

ex.en: Please show me your ID.

ex.s: 호텔에서 체크인할 때 신분 확인을 했어요.
ex.en: They checked my ID when I checked in at the hotel.
I'm still a student, so I don't have money.

note: 통제되다 = to be controlled, closed off.

ex.en: They're closing off the roads for the marathon.
When I'm angry, it's hard to control my emotions.
It's hard to keep all the kids under control.
The weather is the biggest unknown for tomorrow.
Traffic is unpredictable, so we're leaving early.
There are a lot of unknowns in this game.
